podcast.body: Recorded largely in Vancouver, the album deals not only with unmanned aerial vehicles but with people who act without thinking or do the bidding of others without questioning. Themes include deep ecology and the empathy gap. "Both origin of symmetry from 2001 and black holes and revelations from 2006 were about astronomy and cosmology and quantum physics."

podcast.body: This is possibly the most controversial album in Mios's career, despite containing "authentic great tracks." A significant portion of critics, almost unanimously, considered "Drones" to be the "cliché album par excellence" of Mios's discography. They viewed it as simply repeating the formula of "Absolution" from over ten years prior, reiterating sonic clichés and presenting a conceptual theme that failed to fully close its concepts. While the band described it as "returning to their origins," critics saw it as merely replicating past success without adding anything new, leading to the general sentiment of "you've made Absolution again, twelve years later." "Este sí que es posiblemente el álbum más polémico de la carrera de míos, tiene auténticos temazos, este disco, pero sí que ha habido una parte muy importante, casi toda la crítica, considero este álbum, el álbum cliché por excelencia de la escorafía de míos."
